text:
Jamie Chen: Quick benchmark sweep I ran across A100 vs H100 (us-west1 / europe-west1) for Llama-2-13B, MPT-7B, Falcon-40B. Charts: https://internal.redwood/bench/1761234567 (pdf + per-region CSV). TL;DR: H100 wins latency & throughput in almost every config; A100 still cheaper per-hour but worse $/1M tokens because throughput is lower for our common batch sizes.

Sara Patel: awesome — did you run quantized variants?

Jamie Chen: yes, baseline FP16 and 4-bit QAT-style (GPTQ-like). 4-bit gave roughly 1.8–2.1x tokens/sec uplift across models. Quality check: our eval prompt set (1.2k prompts) shows ~0.5–1.2% LM-score drop for Llama-2-13B Q4, negligible for MPT.

Kevin Ortiz: numbers? small table pls (A100 vs H100, prefill, decode, tps, $/1M tokens)

Jamie Chen: pasted quick table (512-token prefill, decode per-token measured at steady-state, cost = infra cost extrapolated from on-demand hour price + infra overhead):
```
Model            | GPU   | Prefill(ms) | Decode(ms/token) | tokens/sec | $/1M tokens
Llama-2-13B      | A100  | 210         | 4.50             | 222        | $17.1
Llama-2-13B      | H100  | 140         | 2.60             | 384        | $12.0
MPT-7B           | A100  | 150         | 2.80             | 357        | $12.0
MPT-7B           | H100  | 100         | 1.80             | 555        | $8.5
Falcon-40B (Q4)  | A100  | 420         | 12.0             | 83         | $60.0
Falcon-40B (Q4)  | H100  | 300         | 7.0              | 142        | $45.0
```
(note: tokens/sec = 1000 / decode(ms/token) for steady stream, rounded; prefill measured for 512 prompt tokens)

Olivia Reed: that gap for Llama-2-13B is pretty big. Kernel notes? which backends did you use?

Jamie Chen: tested cutlass (nv) and Triton kernels where available. Observations: Triton gives ~8–12% better decode on H100 for MPT/Mixed-FFN models, but on A100 cutlass wins for Falcon-40B large matmuls. We also saw kernel choice affect prefill more than per-token decode on long inputs.

Mike Tran: region delta? europe-west1 vs us-west1?

Jamie Chen: region adds ~8–20ms to prefill depending on model size + infra placement. For Llama-2-13B H100 eu-west1 prefill ~155ms (vs 140ms us-west), tokens/sec unchanged (compute same), so $/1M tokens +~8% due to regional infra pricing. Latency-sensitive workloads should prefer regional placement.

Sara Patel: how about batching & p99 impact?

Jamie Chen: batch=1 to batch=8 sweep: tokens/sec improves ~1.6x at batch8 for Llama-2-13B on H100, but p95/p99 decode jumps ~2.5x for small request tails. If your app tolerates small added tail, batching is good for cost efficiency; for interactive chat we recommend batch<=2 and KV-caching.

Kevin Ortiz: any recommendations for Dedicated sizing? e.g., tokens/sec target 50k/s -> how many H100s?

Jamie Chen: rough math: using Llama-2-13B steady 384 t/s (H100) -> 50k/s needs ~130 GPUs raw (50_000 / 384 = 130.2). Add 20% headroom for spikes -> ~156 H100s. With batching & muxing you can shave ~15-25% GPUs depending on request distribution.

bench-bot: automated summary: "H100 median latency 30–45% lower; throughput 1.5–2.0x higher across tested models. 4-bit quantization ~1.8–2.1x throughput uplift with minor eval quality regressions on Llama-2-13B. Kernel choice can add ~10% variance. Region pricing adds ~5–12% to $/token."

Olivia Reed: any weirdness on mixed-precision or memory limits on H100? ECC/instancing?

Jamie Chen: H100 supports larger SMM/instancing, we could run more concurrent contexts which helped Falcon-40B decode. Watch out for per-GPU memory fragmentation when using Q4 + kv-cache for long-context. We applied a small evict-on-alloc heuristic to keep tail latency stable.

Sara Patel: are the raw CSVs in the link usable for our cost automation (redwood-optimize)? I'd like to plug into the model recommendation engine.

Jamie Chen: yes CSV per-run + metadata tag (gpu, kernel, quant, region). File names: bench_1761234567_llama2_13b_h100_eu.csv etc. I can share upload credentials.

Kevin Ortiz: thanks. next actions: (1) Jamie to push the CSVs + simplified summary to #eng-ml-artifacts, (2) Olivia to review kernel tradeoffs for Falcon, (3) Sara to run quality regression sweep on the 1.2k prompts for Q4 = assign.

Jamie Chen: on it. will post artifacts in ~30m and create a short PR with perf config suggestions for Dedicated sizing. :rocket:
